chunks: He will say: 'Alas the woe! Would that I had sent ahead something in my life.'

key_terms.يَا لَيْتَنِي: Alas the woe! / Would that I had

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'Would that I had sent ahead' signify in the context of the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Fajr is often cited to illustrate the irreversible nature of divine decree, emphasizing that regret on the Day of Judgment is futile without prior preparation. It underscores the practical imperative of accumulating 'provisions' (taqwa and good deeds) during the fleeting opportunity of worldly life, a theme central to the concept of *Barzakh* and the final reckoning.
